sections.h2: Selling in Brownsville at a glance
sections.html:
Brownsville sits on the Rio Grande, facing Matamoros, and serves as the seat of Cameron County. Most sales involve three local offices: the appraisal district, the clerk and the tax office. Population was estimated at 192,957 in mid-2025, 3.6% above the 2020 base. Owners live in about 61.7% of homes. The median home value is $139,900 and the median rent is $923.

Since 83.6% of residents age five and older speak another language at home, many families go through contracts and disclosures in two languages. Make sure everyone on the deed understands what they are signing.

sections.h2: How Cameron CAD sets your value
sections.html:
Value comes from the Cameron Appraisal District, while each taxing unit chooses its own rate. The district reappraises every property at least once every three years, and more often where prices move quickly.

A small increase of $1,000 or less needs no notice of appraised value, which is why some owners never see a mailing. Section 23.23 of the Tax Code, in force since January 1, 2008, holds growth in a homestead's assessed value to 10% a year. New rooms, pools and similar improvements sit outside that cap.

Applicants must prove Texas residency, for example with a driver's license, and married owners both apply and show identification. Four exemptions cover a residence: homestead, over-65, disabled person and 100% disabled veteran. A disabled veteran exemption may be placed on any single property the veteran owns instead.

  • You can claim over-65 or disabled in a given year, not both.
  • Where only part of the ownership lives in the house, the account is divided and the exemption is scaled to the qualifying owner's percentage.
  • Adding a pool, garage or room raises the school tax ceiling. A Tax Ceiling Transfer form carries it to a new Texas homestead.

A few exemption types need a new application by April 30 each year. Ask the district which ones apply to you.

The protest goes in writing, due on the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice reached you. Mail, hand delivery and email all work. A mailed one needs a postmark by the deadline.

Once the deadline is gone, nobody at the district or the review board can adjust the value. A hospital stay can be good cause for lateness, but a forgotten date can't. File on time and you receive at least 15 days' notice of a hearing that tends to last about 15 minutes. If the result still looks wrong, the options are district court, binding arbitration or, here in Cameron County, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

  • Name the owner and give the property address or account number.
  • State the issue, such as market value.
  • Attach comparable sales, photos or repair estimates as support.

January 1 fixes both value and the tax lien. Cameron County Tax Office is on East Levee Street, at the same address as the clerk. Call it to learn which taxing units bill your address and what the payoff is.

Key dates for a Brownsville property tax bill
DateWhat happens
January 1Value and the year's lien are set
April 30Some exemption types need a new application
May 15 or 30 days after noticeProtest deadline, whichever is later
Around October 1Bills arrive
February 1Unpaid balances turn delinquent, with a six percent penalty plus one percent interest
After July 1Penalty rises to 12 percent; a unit's attorney may add up to 20 percent

Clear title is impossible with delinquent tax on the books, so pay any balance by closing.

sections.h2: What if the property is headed for a tax sale?
sections.html:
Tax sales are auctions conducted by a constable or a hired agent. No statewide list exists. Look for notices on county websites.

Redemption rights depend on the kind of property. A homestead, farm or mineral owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, at a 25% premium in the first year or 50% in the second, plus costs. Anything else has 180 days and a premium of up to 25%. Money left over after the sale belongs to the former owner, who has two years from the sale date to ask for it.

Valley family land often remains titled to a relative who died decades ago. An affidavit of heirship, sworn and filed with the county clerk, is the quick fix, but no judge reviews it and a title insurer may refuse to rely on it.

Sturdier options: open probate within four years; use a muniment of title when the estate's only debts are liens on the real estate; or rely on a transfer on death deed recorded during the owner's lifetime. Heirs who want an exemption but don't appear on a recorded deed give the appraisal district three items: an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Where a Brownsville deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds, liens, plats and maps are kept by the Cameron County Clerk at 835 E. Levee Street. After a deed is recorded, bring Cameron CAD the instrument, or its volume and page numbers, so the owner of record gets updated.

The state clerk manual sets recording at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page after it, and other fees apply. The clerk can quote the total for your deed.

Brownsville homes range widely in price, and the better route depends on the house. A property in good shape on a popular street can attract several offers from buyers with mortgages, though you will wait through showings, an appraisal and the lender's schedule. A house with a worn roof, a tenant who won't leave or a tax balance that has grown over the years is a different story. Cash buyers expect to price in the repairs, and in return they can often close as soon as the title work is finished.

Ask each buyer for the same three things: the price, who pays closing costs, and the date. Setting offers next to each other on those three lines makes the real difference visible. Then take the best of them to the title company and confirm that nothing on the tax or lien side will change the number.

Start a folder. It should hold your newest bill from the county tax office, the appraisal notice if one arrived, and your Cameron CAD account number with a list of the exemptions on it. If a loan exists, add the payoff. If a tenant lives there, add the lease. If the owner of record has died, add the probate papers or recorded affidavit.

Then ask the clerk's office whether any liens or old instruments are filed against the property. A lien found late can stall a cash closing, so look early. Taken together, these papers let a buyer make a firm offer within days instead of weeks.

Cash offers on Brownsville houses turn on title and taxes. Get yours in writing. Next the title company requests the tax balance, runs a lien search and decides who can sign. A mortgage means a lender payoff figure. An inherited house means settling the probate or affidavit route before anything else.

The deed gets signed, acknowledged and recorded with the county clerk at closing. Your homestead exemption stays behind, and a buyer who will live there files a fresh application. Should a tenant, a guest or a relative still be living in the house, agree on a move-out date with the buyer before the contract is signed.

faqs.q: What does a typical Brownsville home cost?
faqs.a: A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $139,900. What yours brings depends on its condition, lot and street.

faqs.q: Will Cameron CAD always mail a value notice?
faqs.a: No. A notice goes out only when the law calls for one, and an increase of $1,000 or less needs none.

faqs.q: When is a Brownsville appraisal protest due?
faqs.a: By the later of May 15 and 30 days after delivery of the notice. It must be written, and you may mail it, bring it in or email it.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Brownsville deed?
faqs.a: Ask the Cameron County Clerk on East Levee Street. Deeds, surveys and plats are not something the appraisal district hands out.

faqs.q: Does a Brownsville homeowner over 65 get a tax ceiling?
faqs.a: Yes. School taxes on the home usually stay flat for as long as you own and live in it, and the ceiling can follow you to a new Texas homestead.
